content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Lawton

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: The PMP® credential requires a secondary degree plus documented project-management experience, or a high-school diploma with additional experience hours. Review PMI's specific education and professional-experience thresholds to confirm you meet the baseline requirements before enrolling in Granite PM Academy's bootcamp.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual PMP® bootcamp, delivered by active certified practitioners. Attend instructor-led sessions on your schedule, covering the full PMBOK® Guide framework. This formal education satisfies PMI's mandatory contact-hour requirement and prepares you for the exam.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After completing bootcamp coursework, submit your PMP® application directly to PMI, documenting your education and project-management experience. Pay the associated exam fee at application. PMI will verify your credentials before authorizing you to schedule your exam appointment.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Pass the Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources—practice questions, study guides, and instructor office hours—to reinforce PMBOK® concepts and test-taking strategy. Schedule your computer-based exam through Pearson VUE. Pass the PMP® exam to earn your credential.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP® Credential
steps_items.text: The PMP® is valid for three years. During each renewal cycle, earn professional development units (PDUs) through approved project-management training, volunteer work, or knowledge-sharing activities. Renew with PMI before expiration to keep your credential current and strengthen your standing in Lawton's job market.
